name: La Reine Marlene - SIA Project 23 24
description: La Reine Marlene is a company specialized in the sale of home materials and products. The information system manages relationships with suppliers, product proposals, supplier orders, incoming goods, inventory and replenishment, physical and online purchases, deliveries, customer support, and business statistics. Suppliers submit proposals that are evaluated by the administration department. Goods are verified when they arrive at stores. Inventory is monitored and automatic replenishment can be configured. Customers can purchase products online, pay through multiple methods, and track deliveries. Support requests are managed through tickets with automatic assignment, response deadlines and reassignment mechanisms. Company management can analyze data concerning orders, sales, inventory and customer support.

highLevelGoals: To efficiently submit product proposals to La Reine Marlene for evaluation.
To receive timely and clear feedback on submitted product proposals.
To effectively evaluate and manage supplier product proposals for approval or rejection.
To maintain and update system configurations to ensure smooth business operations.
To accurately verify and process incoming goods upon their arrival at the stores.
To continuously monitor inventory levels and ensure stock accuracy.
To ensure that inventory replenishment is automatically triggered when stock levels are low.
To easily browse and purchase desired products through the online platform.
To securely complete payments for online purchases using various available methods.
To accurately track the status and progress of their purchased product deliveries.
To efficiently manage and resolve customer support requests and tickets.
To ensure that customer support requests are responded to within defined deadlines.
To effectively reassign support tickets when necessary to ensure timely resolution.
To gain comprehensive insights into overall business performance through data analysis.
To monitor key operational metrics related to orders, sales, inventory, and customer support.
lowLevelGoals: Supplier initiates the creation of a new product proposal within the system.
Supplier inputs specific product information such as name, description, category, and proposed price into the proposal form.
Supplier uploads relevant images for the proposed product to be included with the proposal.
Supplier attaches any necessary supporting documents, such as certifications or specifications, to the product proposal.
Supplier formally submits the completed product proposal to the system for administrator evaluation.
Supplier checks the current status of a submitted product proposal (e.g., pending, approved, rejected).
Supplier accesses and reads specific feedback comments provided by the administrator on a submitted proposal.
System sends an automated notification to the supplier when the status of their product proposal changes.
Administrator views a list of all product proposals awaiting their review and action.
Administrator opens a specific product proposal to examine all submitted details, images, and documents.
Administrator marks a product proposal as approved, indicating it meets company standards.
Administrator marks a product proposal as rejected, indicating it does not meet company standards.
Administrator provides specific textual feedback or reasons for the approval or rejection of a proposal.
Administrator adds, modifies, or deletes product categories available in the system.
Administrator sets up or adjusts rules and algorithms for product pricing, discounts, or promotions.
Administrator assigns or revokes specific roles and access permissions for different user types within the system.
Administrator configures system-wide notification settings, including triggers and recipients for various events.
Warehouse staff uses a scanner to read the barcode of an incoming product for identification.
Warehouse staff inputs the exact quantity of a specific product received into the system.
Warehouse staff assigns or confirms the physical storage location for newly received goods.
System automatically creates a formal document confirming the receipt of goods after verification.
Warehouse staff checks the real-time quantity of a specific product currently in stock.
Warehouse staff searches for product information using its Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) or name.
System provides a detailed report on current inventory status, including quantities and locations.
Warehouse staff manually corrects discrepancies in the recorded stock count for a product.
Warehouse staff or Administrator defines the minimum stock levels for products that will trigger automatic replenishment.
System sends an automated notification to warehouse staff when a product's stock falls below its defined replenishment threshold.
System automatically creates a purchase order for a product when its stock level meets the replenishment criteria.
Warehouse staff reviews purchase orders that have been automatically created by the system for replenishment.
Customer navigates through the available product categories and listings on the online platform.
Customer uses a search bar to find specific products by entering keywords or phrases.
Customer clicks on a product to see its detailed description, specifications, images, and price.
Customer places a selected product into their virtual shopping cart.
Customer modifies the number of units for a specific product within their shopping cart.
Customer deletes a product from their shopping cart.
Customer initiates the checkout process from their shopping cart to finalize the purchase.
Customer chooses their preferred payment method (e.g., credit card, digital wallet) during checkout.
Customer inputs necessary payment details, such as credit card number or login credentials for a payment gateway.
Customer authorizes the payment to complete the purchase.
System sends an automated notification to the customer confirming successful payment.
Customer accesses a list of all their past and current online orders.
Customer obtains the tracking number and carrier details for a specific order.
Customer views the current shipping status of their order (e.g., 'shipped', 'in transit', 'delivered').
System sends automated notifications to the customer regarding changes in their order's delivery status.
Customer Support Agent accesses a list of all unresolved customer support requests.
Customer Support Agent takes ownership of an unassigned support ticket.
Customer Support Agent records private notes or updates related to a ticket for internal team reference.
Customer Support Agent composes and sends a reply to the customer regarding their support request.
Customer Support Agent changes the status of a support ticket (e.g., 'in progress', 'awaiting customer', 'resolved').
Customer Support Agent marks a support ticket as resolved and closed.
Customer Support Agent sorts and filters support tickets based on their priority level or approaching deadline.
System sends an automated alert to the Customer Support Agent when a ticket's response deadline is approaching.
System automatically records the time taken by an agent to provide the first response to a customer support ticket.
Customer Support Agent transfers a support ticket to a different individual agent for resolution.
Customer Support Agent transfers a support ticket to a specialized department or team.
Customer Support Agent checks the current number of active tickets assigned to other agents or departments.
Company Manager requests and views a report detailing sales figures, trends, and revenue over a specified period.
Company Manager accesses data and statistics related to new customer sign-ups and acquisition channels.
Company Manager views a dashboard summarizing key financial performance indicators and profitability metrics.
Company Manager downloads raw or aggregated business data in a compatible format for use with external analytical tools.
Company Manager monitors the number of orders placed within a recent time frame in real-time.
Company Manager views the rate at which inventory is sold and replaced over a period.
Company Manager views the percentage of customer support tickets successfully resolved within a given period.
Company Manager views graphical representations of sales data over various timeframes to identify trends.

baselineCritiques.actors: The identified actors are accurate and cover the main roles described in the system (Suppliers, Administration, Warehouse/Inventory, Customers, Support, and Management). However, the description explicitly mentions "physical and online purchases." While "Customer" covers the online aspect, the physical purchase process typically involves a "Store Clerk" or "Sales Associate" who assists customers in-store and processes payments, distinct from the online self-service flow. Omitting this role is a minor gap given the explicit mention of physical purchases.
baselineCritiques.highLevelGoals: The provided high-level goals are comprehensive and accurately reflect the functional requirements described in the software description. They cover all major actors (Supplier, Administrator, Warehouse Staff, Customer, Customer Support Agent, Company Manager) and their respective responsibilities (proposals, evaluation, inventory, purchasing, support, analytics). The goals are functional in nature, focusing on the 'what' and 'why' of the system's capabilities without delving into technical implementation details. There are no contradictions with the description, and no significant functional areas appear to be omitted. The truncation in the text (e.g., "l…", "supp…") is likely a formatting artifact and does not affect the semantic correctness of the goals.
baselineCritiques.lowLevelGoals: The low-level goals are comprehensive, well-structured, and accurately reflect the functional requirements derived from the high-level goals and software description. They correctly map to the defined actors and cover all major processes (proposals, inventory, e-commerce, support, analytics). There are no contradictions, out-of-context items, or significant omissions. The goals are appropriately granular for a low-level specification.

hlg_2a6d54c79c47d036_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Monitor Inventory Levels' is supported by the documentation, which states that 'Inventory is monitored'. The material outcome set of the HLG is {monitor levels, ensure accuracy}. The reconstructed HLG' aggregates the LLGs into {view stock, search product, generate report, adjust stock}. While 'view stock' and 'adjust stock' align with monitoring and accuracy, the HLG' introduces 'search product' and 'generate report' which are not explicitly entailed by the generic 'monitor' description, nor does the HLG explicitly cover 'report generation'. However, the HLG is a valid high-level abstraction for the inventory monitoring capability. The reconstruction is a lossless aggregate of the children but expands the scope slightly beyond the strict 'monitoring' label to include reporting and search. Since the HLG is valid and the reconstruction covers the core intent plus specific operational details, it is a partial overlap where the HLG is a valid parent. The LLGs need evaluation to ensure they don't drift into unsupported territory (e.g., if 'search' is considered a distinct capability from 'monitoring'). Voting result 2/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The decomposition is incomplete. The parent HLG 'Monitor Inventory Levels' explicitly includes the goal to 'ensure stock accuracy'. While llg_004 allows for manual correction of discrepancies, it does not cover the proactive monitoring aspect of accuracy, such as identifying or flagging low stock levels or discrepancies for attention. The sibling HLG 'Ensure Automatic Replenishment' handles the *triggering* of replenishment, but the *monitoring* of levels to detect when they are low (the prerequisite for that trigger) is a distinct capability of the 'Monitor Inventory Levels' goal that is absent from the current LLGs. Without a capability to identify low stock or discrepancies, the system cannot effectively 'ensure stock accuracy' or support the replenishment workflow. Therefore, an essential capability is missing.

'Receive automated notifications' is a system-initiated outcome not explicitly stated in the original HLG description, though implied by 'track'. The original HLG is valid and supported, so it should be kept, and the LLGs need evaluation to determine if the broader scope in HLG' (specifically notifications and order history access) is correctly decomposed or if the HLG description needs to be broadened to match the actual system capabilities (which the LLGs suggest). hlg_7c8b3b5d280cf49c_001.rationale:
Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The documentation supports 'response deadlines' as a feature of support tickets. The original HLG 'Meet Response Deadlines' expresses the outcome of ensuring requests are responded to within these deadlines. The LLGs decompose this into: (1) viewing tickets by priority/deadline (agent action), (2) receiving deadline reminders (system action), and (3) logging response time (system action). The reconstruction HLG' accurately aggregates these three specific capabilities. However, HLG' describes the *mechanisms* (sorting, alerting, logging) rather than the *outcome* (meeting the deadline). While the mechanisms support the outcome, the reconstruction does not explicitly entail the successful completion of the response within the deadline, which is the core of the original HLG. Conversely, the original HLG implies the use of these mechanisms. This is a PARTIAL_OVERLAP because HLG' covers the operational steps but not the final state of 'meeting' the deadline, whereas the original HLG is the goal state. The parent is valid and supported by the documentation. The LLGs need evaluation to ensure they correctly implement the goal. Voting result 2/3 for KEEP_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The parent HLG 'Meet Response Deadlines' requires ensuring support requests are responded to within defined deadlines. The documentation explicitly states that support requests are managed with 'response deadlines'. 

1. **llg_001 (View Tickets by Priority/Deadline)**: Supported. Sorting/filtering by deadline is a necessary mechanism for an agent to identify which tickets are at risk of missing deadlines, directly contributing to the goal of meeting them. 
2. **llg_002 (Receive Deadline Reminder Notification)**: Supported. The documentation mentions 'response deadlines'. Automated alerts for approaching deadlines are a standard and necessary entailment for 'ensuring' deadlines are met, as passive tracking is insufficient for proactive management. It is not an invented feature but a direct operationalization of the deadline constraint. 
3. **llg_003 (Log Agent Response Time)**: Supported. To 'ensure' deadlines are met, the system must track performance against those deadlines. Recording the time taken to respond is the fundamental metric for verifying compliance with the 'response deadlines' mentioned in the documentation. It is not merely optional analytics but the verification mechanism for the parent goal. 

All LLGs are distinct, non-redundant, and directly entailed by the requirement to manage and meet response deadlines. No essential capabilities are missing, and no LLGs are unsupported or misleading.

However, the original HLG is not strictly equivalent to HLG' because HLG' explicitly lists 'reassign' and 'retrieve' as distinct capabilities, whereas the original HLG's description 'manage and resolve' is broader and does not explicitly entail the specific operational granularity of 'reassigning' or 'retrieving' in a way that proves bidirectional entailment of every material clause without interpretation. More importantly, the sibling branch 'Reassign Support Tickets' (hlg_367131c408293017_001) explicitly covers the reassignment capability. hlg_917f60a17784d769_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Suppliers to initiate the creation of, populate with specific product information (name, description, category, proposed price), relevant images, and necessary supporting documents (certifications, specifications), and formally submit new product proposals for administrator evaluation.
hlg_917f60a17784d769_001.rationale: llg_001 establishes the capability for a Supplier to initiate the creation of a new product proposal. llg_002 specifies the capability for a Supplier to input core textual product information (name, description, category, proposed price) into the proposal form. llg_003 adds the capability for a Supplier to upload relevant images for the proposed product. llg_004 introduces the capability for a Supplier to attach necessary supporting documents (certifications, specifications) to the product proposal. llg_005 defines the final action of a Supplier formally submitting the completed product proposal for administrator evaluation.

hlg_9204cf42c20db99d_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable suppliers to check the current status of their submitted product proposals, access and read specific feedback comments provided by the administrator on those proposals, and receive automated notifications from the system when the status of their product proposals changes.
hlg_9204cf42c20db99d_001.rationale: llg_001 contributes the capability for the supplier to actively check the current status of a submitted product proposal. llg_002 adds the capability for the supplier to access and read specific feedback comments provided by the administrator on a submitted proposal. llg_003 introduces the system's proactive capability to send automated notifications to the supplier when the status of their product proposal changes.

hlg_01a9383eaeacbaa1_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Administrator reviews and takes action on product proposals by viewing a list of those awaiting review, opening and examining specific proposal details, images, and documents, and subsequently marking proposals as approved or rejected, while also providing specific textual feedback or reasons for the decision.
hlg_01a9383eaeacbaa1_001.rationale: llg_001 contributes the capability for the Administrator to view a list of all product proposals awaiting their review and action. llg_002 adds the capability for the Administrator to open a specific product proposal to examine all submitted details, images, and documents. llg_003 provides the capability for the Administrator to mark a product proposal as approved. llg_004 provides the capability for the Administrator to mark a product proposal as rejected. llg_005 adds the capability for the Administrator to provide specific textual feedback or reasons for the approval or rejection of a proposal.

hlg_78422a9ed5decd1f_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Administrator adds, modifies, and deletes product categories; sets up and adjusts rules and algorithms for product pricing, discounts, and promotions; assigns and revokes specific roles and access permissions for different user types; and configures system-wide notification settings, including triggers and recipients for various events.
hlg_78422a9ed5decd1f_001.rationale: llg_001 contributes the capability for the Administrator to perform CRUD operations on product categories. llg_002 adds the capability for the Administrator to set up and adjust rules and algorithms for product pricing, discounts, or promotions. llg_003 provides the capability for the Administrator to assign and revoke specific roles and access permissions for different user types. llg_004 contributes the capability for the Administrator to configure system-wide notification settings, including triggers and recipients for various events. All these distinct administrative configuration capabilities are aggregated into the high-level goal without loss of detail.

hlg_759017a9abeaa4da_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Warehouse staff identifies incoming products by scanning barcodes, inputs their received quantities, and assigns or confirms their physical storage locations, while the system automatically creates a formal document confirming the receipt of these goods after verification.
hlg_759017a9abeaa4da_001.rationale: llg_001 contributes the capability for warehouse staff to identify incoming products using a scanner to read barcodes. llg_002 adds the capability for warehouse staff to input the exact quantity of received products into the system. llg_003 introduces the capability for warehouse staff to assign or confirm the physical storage location for newly received goods. llg_004 provides the capability for the system to automatically create a formal document confirming the receipt of goods after verification.

hlg_2a6d54c79c47d036_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Warehouse Staff to view the current quantity of all products, search for specific product inventory details by SKU or name, identify and view products below predefined reorder thresholds or with reported physical/system count discrepancies, manually update specific product stock quantities to correct discrepancies, and generate reports detailing current inventory levels, movements, or discrepancies for a specified period.
hlg_2a6d54c79c47d036_001.rationale: The reconstructed high-level goal comprehensively captures all distinct functional capabilities provided to the Warehouse Staff by the low-level goals. llg_001 contributes the ability to view the current quantity of all products. llg_002 adds the capability to search for and view specific product inventory details using SKU or name. llg_003 introduces the functionality to generate reports on inventory levels, movements, or discrepancies for a specified period. llg_004 provides the ability to manually update stock quantities for specific products to correct discrepancies. Finally, llg_005 adds the capability to identify and view products based on reorder thresholds or reported discrepancies between physical and system counts.

hlg_dfa666d466a9c65b_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Warehouse staff or Administrators to define minimum stock levels for products to trigger automatic replenishment, and empower the System to detect when product stock falls below these defined thresholds, send automated notifications to staff, automatically create purchase orders for replenishment, and allow Warehouse staff to review these automatically created purchase orders.
hlg_dfa666d466a9c65b_001.rationale: The reconstructed high-level goal integrates all distinct functional capabilities from the low-level goals. llg_001 contributes the capability for 'Warehouse staff or Administrators to define minimum stock levels for products to trigger automatic replenishment'. llg_002 adds the system's ability to 'detect when product stock falls below these defined thresholds' and 'send automated notifications to staff'. llg_003 introduces the system's capability to 'automatically create purchase orders for replenishment'. Finally, llg_004 completes the scope by adding the capability for 'Warehouse staff to review these automatically created purchase orders'.

hlg_67a02c7c0ac318df_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Customer discovers products by navigating categories and searching, views product details, manages a virtual shopping cart by adding, modifying quantities, and deleting products, and initiates the checkout process to finalize a purchase on an online platform.
hlg_67a02c7c0ac318df_001.rationale: The reconstructed high-level goal encompasses all distinct functional capabilities present in the low-level goals. llg_001 contributes the ability for a Customer to discover products by navigating categories and listings. llg_002 adds the capability for a Customer to discover products using a search bar with keywords. llg_003 provides the functionality for a Customer to view detailed product information including description, specifications, images, and price. llg_004 introduces the action of a Customer placing a product into their virtual shopping cart. llg_005 specifies the Customer's ability to modify the quantity of a product within the shopping cart. llg_006 details the Customer's option to delete a product from their shopping cart. Finally, llg_007 completes the scope by enabling the Customer to initiate the checkout process from the shopping cart to finalize a purchase. All these capabilities collectively describe the customer's journey from product discovery to initiating a purchase on an online platform.

hlg_07d5a6d1a2c45846_001.rationale: llg_001 contributes the capability for customers to select their preferred payment method during checkout. llg_002 adds the capability for customers to input the required payment details. llg_003 includes the capability for customers to authorize the payment to finalize their purchase. llg_004 introduces the capability for the system to send automated notifications to customers confirming successful payment.

hlg_22d9553eba25ee3e_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: The customer can retrieve initial shipment details, including the specific tracking number and carrier, and query the current status of a purchased product delivery using its tracking information.
hlg_22d9553eba25ee3e_001.rationale: llg_001 contributes the capability for the customer to retrieve the specific tracking number, carrier, and initial shipment details for a purchased product delivery. llg_002 contributes the capability for the customer to query the system to obtain the current status (e.g., 'In Transit', 'Out for Delivery', 'Delivered') of a specific product delivery using its tracking information.

hlg_e2dd6affb4d30d3d_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: To enable customer support agents and departments to manage the lifecycle and communication for support tickets, specifically by retrieving lists of open and assigned tickets, assigning and reassigning tickets to agents, changing responsible departments, modifying ticket statuses (including resolving and closing), and composing and sending textual responses to customers.
hlg_e2dd6affb4d30d3d_001.rationale: The reconstructed high-level goal integrates all distinct capabilities provided by the low-level goals. llg_001 contributes the ability to retrieve lists of open and assigned support tickets. llg_002 adds the capability to assign unassigned or newly created tickets to agents. llg_003 provides the functionality to reassign existing tickets to different agents. llg_004 introduces the ability to change the department responsible for a ticket. llg_005 contributes the communication aspect, allowing agents to compose and send textual responses to customers. llg_006 enables the modification of a ticket's current status through its lifecycle. hlg_dfa666d466a9c65b_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The documentation supports automatic replenishment configuration and monitoring. The original HLG 'Ensure Automatic Replenishment' focuses on the system's automatic triggering mechanism. The reconstruction HLG' aggregates all LLGs, including 'Set Replenishment Thresholds', 'Receive Low Stock Alert', and 'View Auto-Generated Purchase Orders'. While the original HLG implies the outcome of replenishment, it does not explicitly state the user-facing capabilities of setting thresholds or viewing orders, which are distinct functional outcomes in the LLGs. However, the core intention of the HLG is the automatic process itself. The sibling 'Monitor Inventory Levels' covers general monitoring but not the specific automatic replenishment workflow (thresholds, PO generation). The HLG is valid but the reconstruction is broader, capturing the full scope of the branch's LLGs which includes configuration and review steps not explicitly in the HLG name/description. This is a PARTIAL_OVERLAP where the HLG is a valid subset of the reconstructed scope. The HLG is supported and valid, so it should be kept, and the LLGs need evaluation to ensure they align with the HLG's scope or if the HLG needs to be broadened to explicitly include the configuration/review aspects if they are considered essential to the 'Ensure' outcome. Given the HLG is 'Ensure', the configuration is a prerequisite. The reconstruction is a lossless aggregate. The relationship is PARTIAL_OVERLAP because HLG' includes explicit user actions (set, view) that are not explicitly in the HLG text, though they support the HLG. The HLG is valid. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The decomposition is incomplete and contains unsupported content. The parent HLG 'Ensure Automatic Replenishment' is explicitly defined in the project description as 'automatic replenishment can be configured'. This implies the core capability is the configuration of the automatic process itself (e.g., enabling the feature, setting rules), which is distinct from merely setting a numeric threshold (llg_001). More critically, llg_004 ('Receive Low Stock Alert') is unsupported. The documentation states that inventory is monitored and replenishment is automatic, but it does not mention notifications, alerts, or any mechanism for the Warehouse Staff to be notified of low stock. The actor's description ('monitors inventory') implies active checking or system visibility, not necessarily push notifications. Furthermore, llg_005 ('View Auto-Generated Purchase Orders') overlaps with the sibling HLG 'Manage System Configurations' or potentially 'Analyze Business Performance' if viewed as a review process, but more importantly, the documentation does not explicitly state that Warehouse Staff review these specific auto-generated orders; it only states that replenishment is triggered. The essential capability of 'Configuring Automatic Replenishment' (the act of enabling/setting up the automation logic) is missing, and the notification capability is invented.

hlg_dfa666d466a9c65b_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable Warehouse Staff to configure the automatic replenishment feature by defining its operational parameters and stock thresholds, and to access and review automatically generated purchase orders for replenishment; concurrently, enable the system to continuously monitor inventory, identify when stock levels fall below predefined thresholds, and automatically initiate the creation of purchase orders upon detection of low stock.
hlg_dfa666d466a9c65b_001.rationale: llg_001 contributes the capability for Warehouse Staff to enable the automatic replenishment feature and define its operational parameters, including stock thresholds. llg_002 adds the system's capability to continuously monitor inventory and identify when stock levels fall below predefined thresholds. llg_003 provides the system's capability to automatically initiate the creation of a purchase order when low stock levels are detected. llg_004 includes the capability for Warehouse Staff to access and review purchase orders that have been automatically generated by the system for replenishment.

hlg_371f4b7489a97fe4_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: The system shall enable the Company Manager to generate reports detailing metrics across sales, order fulfillment, inventory, and customer support for a specified period; retrieve and display key customer acquisition metrics and profitability indicators via a dashboard; and export raw or aggregated business data, including sales, order, inventory, and customer support records, for external analytical tools.
hlg_371f4b7489a97fe4_001.rationale: This High-Level Goal is a lossless reconstruction of the provided Low-Level Goals. llg_001 contributes the capability for the Company Manager to generate detailed reports on operational metrics (sales, order fulfillment, inventory, customer support) for a specified period. llg_002 adds the capability for the Company Manager to retrieve and display key customer acquisition metrics. llg_003 introduces the capability for the Company Manager to retrieve and display profitability indicators via a dashboard. Finally, llg_004 provides the distinct capability for the Company Manager to export raw or aggregated business data (sales, order, inventory, customer support records) in a machine-readable format for external analytical tools.

hlg_dfa666d466a9c65b_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The documentation supports 'Inventory is monitored and automatic replenishment can be configured.' The original HLG outcomes are {ensure automatic replenishment triggered when stock is low}. The reconstructed HLG' outcomes are {configure replenishment parameters, monitor inventory, detect low stock, trigger purchase order generation, view auto-generated purchase orders}. HLG' entails HLG (triggering is a core part of the reconstruction). However, HLG' adds 'configure' and 'view' capabilities which are not explicitly stated in the original HLG description, although they are supported by the documentation and the LLGs. The original HLG is a valid, supported, and precise statement of the functional outcome. The reconstruction is a lossless aggregate of the LLGs, which includes the configuration and viewing steps that support the main goal. Since the original HLG is valid and the reconstruction covers the same functional domain with additional detail from the LLGs, the relationship is PARTIAL_OVERLAP (HLG' is broader/more detailed than the concise HLG). The parent is valid, so it should be kept. The LLGs need evaluation to ensure they correctly implement the goal. Voting result 2/3 for KEEP_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The LLGs accurately decompose the parent HLG 'Ensure Automatic Replenishment'. llg_001 supports the configuration of thresholds, llg_002 covers the monitoring and detection of low stock, llg_003 addresses the automatic triggering of purchase orders, and llg_004 allows the Warehouse Staff to review the generated orders. All capabilities are explicitly grounded in the project description ('Inventory is monitored and automatic replenishment can be configured') and the parent HLG description. There are no unsupported additions, redundancies, or missing essential capabilities.
